rationale: A wins because it is more disciplined about what the facts can actually carry. Its strongest line is the adult warning under the Adobe angle: "do not infer the motive — the fact block only states the launch follows the collapse"; that is the difference between a press angle and fan fiction in a blazer. B has sharper raw inventory, especially "The Fortune 500 design tool is now asking to write production code," but it also drags in "the IPO clock is unstated" and several production-code assumptions the update does not support.
gaps_in_A: "Figma's first move after the Adobe deal died" overclaims. The update says the launch follows the collapsed acquisition, not that it is the first move or a strategic response.
"shippable React code" is a little too confident. The facts say working front-end code; shippable is exactly what the proof section says still needs testing.
A misses the enterprise procurement/security angle hiding in "most Fortune 500 companies" plus code export. That is a real fourth lens, not padding.
gaps_in_B: "the IPO clock is unstated" puts IPO absence in the headline. The fact is useful as a boundary, not as bait for a story you cannot substantiate.
"Design-to-code has been promised for a decade and has repeatedly produced unmaintainable output" may be true, but it is not in the supplied update. Do not smuggle market history in without evidence.

"If a tool already inside most Fortune 500 companies starts emitting code that ships to production" stacks assumptions: Figma usage is not Make adoption, and exported code is not shipped production code.
"Next step: newsjack-detector" is the wrong lead move for a launch-angle set. Pick the angle, verify the proof, then run journalist-fit-check.
